limits: The Monte Carlo is a model of resource/07's assumptions, not a forecast: i.i.d. Student-t(4) daily returns with constant Sharpe and vol, no volatility clustering, no regime dependence, no funding or fee lines (they are inside the memo's net Sharpe). It reproduces T6g's pause probabilities within a few points but understates them (zero edge 33% vs 45% within 2 years), so every drawdown and pause figure is a lower bound.

The daily book's 19% vol is the full-sample T1 figure for TV 0.40; the paper book has realised only 10.7%/yr in 19 days at 0.11-0.64x gross because signals have been weak. The daily book is given the same Sharpe grid as the weekly book; resource/07 puts the daily cadence about 0.13 Sharpe above the weekly, which would shift the daily results toward the next-higher Sharpe cell.

The tax model is a linear fit of six T6b years of the design line (rmse 3.3 pp per-segment, 9.5 pp per-coin-day), intercept scaled by vol for the daily book; a daily-rebalanced book's 'segments' are shorter, so its per-segment line probably sits between the two fits (resource/08's daily panel-B line implies gross gains of about 32% at +13.6% net vs the fit's 37%). Slab tax ignores cess, surcharge and the 4-year carry-forward limit. None of this is tax advice; the CA opinion is Gate 0.

Whole-contract rounding, the 30%-on-venue margin dynamics and the BTC/BNB round-to-zero effect at $1,000 are not modelled (resource/07: rounding is noise from $1,000; at $500 gross is 75% of intended).

FD rate 6.5-7% and after-tax 4.7% are resource/07's [UNVERIFIED] figures; every prop-firm fact is [UNVERIFIED]/[THIRD-PARTY] per resource/07, and the prop EV per year uses the memo's 17-month cycle (my $0.9-1.75k/yr per $100k account vs the memo's $1.3-1.8k).

The ADA market-maker comparator rests on 6.27 days of venue cash-flow (+$33.29), a revocable Scalper Offer fee of 1.25 bps, an open +496 ADA position at the end, and DATA.txt's capacity statement (2.5-3% of $595k/day); it was not re-measured here.

The realised vol of the daily paper book is 10.7%/yr by rebalance-to-rebalance equity (18 returns x sqrt(365)); the lead's 10.1% is a different convention. The 19-day return percentile (34-36th) is the same either way.
